title: IFFI opens in Goa tonight with Ricky Kej orchestra; Uttam Kumar centenary among tributes
dek: The 57th International Film Festival of India begins at the Shyama Prasad Mukherjee Stadium with Pawlikowski's 'Fatherland'. Two Bengali films are in the Indian Panorama and a Bengali debutant is in the running for an award.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
The 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) opens in Goa on Friday evening with a ceremony at the Dr Shyama Prasad Mukherjee Stadium near Panaji, featuring a symphonic orchestra led by the composer Ricky Kej, before the screening of the opening film, Fatherland, by the Polish director Paweł Pawlikowski.

The nine-day festival, which runs until 28 November under the theme "Stories Without Borders", will also mark the birth centenary of the Bengali screen star Uttam Kumar, among other figures of Indian cinema, the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting said in releases issued through the Press Information Bureau (PIB). The ceremony is due to begin at 5.30 pm, according to reports.

## The ceremony

The evening opens with a sound and light presentation, followed by the National Song and National Anthem, and the lighting of the lamp and watering of a tulsi plant, "symbolising light, life and new beginnings", the ministry said in its release on Thursday. Kej, a three-time Grammy winner, will lead an orchestral piece titled "A World of Cinema Through Music", followed by "Music Without Borders", with musicians from several countries, and "Beyond the Frame", a dance built around the peacock emblem of the festival.

Goa Chief Minister Pramod Sawant and senior officials of the ministry are due to speak. Ravi Kishan, the actor and MP, festival director Ashutosh Gowariker and the filmmakers Madhur Bhandarkar and Aanand L. Rai are among those listed to attend. The juries for the International Competition, chaired by Rai, and for the Indian Panorama, chaired by Bhandarkar for features and Himansu Sekhar Khatua, a former director of Kolkata's Satyajit Ray Film and Television Institute, for non-features, will be introduced on stage. A presentation will mark 20 years of the Film Bazaar, now called WAVES Film Bazaar, the festival's market for buyers and producers.

## Bengal at the festival

IFFI 2026 "will celebrate the birth centenaries of eminent personalities of Indian cinema", the ministry said, naming the filmmakers Shakti Samanta and Raj Khosla, the actors Uttam Kumar, Suryakant Mandhare, Prem Nazir and Raj Kumar, and the composers O.P. Nayyar and Ravi. Uttam Kumar, born in Calcutta in 1926, was the leading man of Bengali cinema for nearly three decades; Shakti Samanta, also born in 1926, directed him in Amanush and Anand Ashram, both made in Bengali and Hindi.

The Indian Panorama, 76 films in 18 languages, includes the Bengali feature Pagla Ghora, directed by Sekhar Das, and the Bengali non-feature film Kathar Katha by Dhritisree Sarkar, according to reports. Samarpan Sengupta's Pratyabartan is among the nominees for the award for best debut by an Indian director, according to reports.

## What else is on

The festival will screen more than 150 international films from 86 countries on 13 screens at four locations, in Panaji, Porvorim, Margao and Ponda, with about 4,000 seats in all, the ministry said. Spain is the Country of Honour and Russia the Partner Country, and the festival has a new section devoted to films from the BRICS countries. The Kala Academy will host 14 masterclasses, panels and conversations from 21 to 27 November.

Fatherland follows the German writer Thomas Mann and his daughter Erika on a journey through divided Germany in 1949; Pawlikowski shared the Best Director award at Cannes this year for it. The mid-festival film is I Matter, by the Romanian director Alina Șerban, and the festival closes on 28 November with We Are All Strangers, by Singapore's Anthony Chen, when the Golden Peacock for best film and five Silver Peacock awards will be announced.
